Deliverable: A version-pinned capability inventory and migration-safe extension map
Acceptance checks: Inventory matches pinned main commit; each existing service has an integration owner; no duplicate database or identity subsystem proposed; undocumented assumptions flagged.
Demonstration: Generate an inventory JSON and cross-reference report from the checked-out repository.

Stage name: Canonical semantic type and Cog contracts
Deliverable: Versioned semantic schemas for tool, capability, implementation, installation, invocation and evidence
Acceptance checks: Reject shorthand Type identifiers; reject unknown/unregistered data Type refs, invalid inheritance and Ember violations; detect incompatible schema evolution; serialize/deserialize deterministically.
Demonstration: Round-trip a SearchQuery → SearchResults Cog and a tool invocation receipt.

Deliverable: Signed, immutable invocation/result/receipt envelope and lifecycle schema
Acceptance checks: Canonical hashes stable on repeat; altered inputs or policy revision invalidate reuse; partial execution never appears verified; payloads over size limits are rejected.
Demonstration: Replay an immutable read-only invocation and inspect the linked receipt chain.

Stage name: Build matrix and stage acceptance harness
Deliverable: Stage-aware CI, disposable integration services and machine-readable gate reports
Acceptance checks: Fail if mandated DB/sandbox suite skipped; never treat synthetic fixtures as live qualification; prove migration compatibility; preserve all existing test suites.
Demonstration: One command produces a P01 gate report and a reproducible failing negative test.

Deliverable: Fully tested stdio MCP client for curated servers
Acceptance checks: Fixture MCP server passes discovery, calls, tool errors, pagination, server crash, oversized payload and cancellation tests; blocked tools cannot be called by guessing IDs.
Demonstration: Invoke a local calculator MCP server in a confined workspace.

Prerequisites: T02.1,T01.3; security design review before remote calls
Deliverable: Remote MCP transport with authenticated resource-scoped access
Acceptance checks: Mismatched protocol fails clearly; expired/wrong-audience OAuth token rejected; untrusted redirects blocked; 401/403 and disconnect produce correct statuses; reconnect does not repeat writes.
Demonstration: Call a controlled remote read-only MCP endpoint using scoped OAuth test credentials.

Deliverable: Typed CLI/process adapter running only through approved executors
Acceptance checks: Reject arbitrary host executable, paths outside registered workspace, shell injection and environment leakage; kill child process trees at timeout; stream bounded progress.
Demonstration: Run git status, python -V and a controlled failing command from workspace tooling.

Stage name: HTTP, SDK, GraphQL and gRPC adapters
Deliverable: Common schema-checked API adapter framework
Acceptance checks: Malformed schemas, hostile redirects, unbounded pagination, malformed response bodies and timeout retry paths fail safely; idempotent reads cache correctly; writes are never blindly retried.
Demonstration: Use a mocked versioned REST service and a real local GraphQL/gRPC fixture.

Deliverable: Policy decision service with explainable authorization
Acceptance checks: Default deny; parent grant cannot be broadened by child; privilege escalation by modifying tool metadata rejected; deny decisions logged without leaking secrets.
Demonstration: Show authorized search and denied cloud-delete operations for same agent.

Deliverable: Enforced filesystem/network boundary for local and remote tool tasks
Acceptance checks: Traversal, symlink, junction, mount, /proc leakage, localhost metadata probing and redirect-to-internal-IP are denied; host files cannot be read/written; unqualified platform cannot run untrusted workloads.
Demonstration: Adversarial fixture attempts workspace escape and forbidden network destinations.

Deliverable: Non-exportable scoped credential acquisition and usage
Acceptance checks: Secret scanner finds no credentials in traces/artifacts; incorrect identity/recipient rejected; child tool cannot read broker storage; key rotation invalidates stale rights; no unsupported custody profile claims.
Demonstration: Call an authenticated test API while the agent sees only an opaque credential handle.

Deliverable: First end-to-end authorized tool runner
Acceptance checks: 100 simulated worker crashes result in no unauthorized repeat of side-effecting call; concurrent claims do not double execute; denied approval means zero side effects; read-only invocations replay safely.
Demonstration: An operator approves a restricted tool invocation from CLI/API; job/receipt appears in WebSocket replay.

Stage name: Curated registry and trusted package catalog
Deliverable: Local signed/version-pinned capability and adapter catalog
Acceptance checks: Unpinned or unsigned high-risk package rejected by policy; stale manifest flagged; malicious package cannot gain network/filesystem grants by self-description.
Demonstration: List and inspect 20 curated adapters without installing all dependencies.

Stage name: MCP discovery, rescan and schema reconciliation
Deliverable: Incremental MCP search and dynamic catalog updates
Acceptance checks: Discovery is deterministic across reconnects; tool removal invalidates planner references; changed schema requires revalidation; list pagination returns every permitted tool.
Demonstration: Add a fake MCP tool during an active session; see tool appear without restarting the agent.

Deliverable: Semantic + symbolic selector with cost/security filtering
Acceptance checks: A golden set of 40 requests routes to expected capability class; permission-disallowed option never ranks as executable; cold discovery bounded by token/tool budget.
Demonstration: Ask for screenshot inspection, satisfiability solving and commit inspection without naming vendors.

Stage name: Versioning, health, revocation and install lifecycle
Deliverable: Operator lifecycle APIs and circuit breakers
Acceptance checks: Rolling update preserves old active runs; revoked instance is denied immediately to new calls; rollback restores previous manifest without corrupting receipts; health state is visible.
Demonstration: Disable a known-bad test tool during queued invocations and verify safe behavior.

Stage name: Search provider adapters and result normalization
Deliverable: Multi-provider search capability with source timestamps
Acceptance checks: Mocked quota failure falls back when policy allows; duplicates deduplicated but source lineage retained; restricted result providers cannot silently exfiltrate sensitive queries.
Demonstration: Compare two providers for a technical research query and save independent result sets.

Stage name: Fetch, extraction and canonical source artifacts
Deliverable: Web fetch/crawler with robust content provenance
Acceptance checks: Correctly extracts authored text from HTML, PDF and JSON fixtures; preserves citation spans and source hashes; rejects zip bombs, huge pages and private-network redirects.
Demonstration: Follow search results and answer with verifiable document-location citations.

Deliverable: Domain source connectors with query contracts
Acceptance checks: DOI resolution and duplicate author/title matching work; retractions/corrections represented; unsupported endpoints degrade explicitly; rate-limits respected.
Demonstration: Retrieve a paper and its linked metadata from two independent sources.

Deliverable: Reproducible research workflow and contradiction matrix
Acceptance checks: Planted conflicting claims produce an unresolved state; old news not mislabeled current; every quoted claim has traceable source offsets; zero fabricated citations in gold fixture.
Demonstration: Research a contested technical specification and show supported vs unresolved claims.

Deliverable: Managed isolated browser sessions via Playwright MCP/CLI
Acceptance checks: Two workspaces cannot read each others cookies; malicious webpage instructions cannot authorize new tool calls; downloads remain under workspace; session recovery does not invent form submission status.
Demonstration: Automate an internal test application from login through read-only dashboard export.

Deliverable: CDP-based debugging and performance capability
Acceptance checks: Captures and attributes a deliberately failing request; rejects debugger connection outside permitted sessions; large traces redacted and bounded.
Demonstration: Locate a simulated CORS, 404 or frontend JavaScript failure.

Stage name: Visual regression, accessibility and desktop fallback
Deliverable: Multimodal browser result and UI test adapters
Acceptance checks: Detect known 1-pixel/large-layout regressions with tuned thresholds; keyboard-only path tested; false-positive baseline reported; no raw browser profile credentials exported.
Demonstration: Compare UI screenshots and explain visually detected vs DOM-detected changes.

Stage name: Browser reliability benchmark and test fixtures
Deliverable: Browser action benchmark with deterministic replay
Acceptance checks: >=95% deterministic success on own stable fixture at pinned environment after agreed retries; zero unauthorized form submissions; reproducible traces for every failed case.
Demonstration: Dashboard of browser methods and sample CI artifact.

Deliverable: Repository-host adapters with scoped tools
Acceptance checks: Read-only PAT cannot create PR; pagination complete; webhook replays deduplicated; pull request operations bound to exact branch and current revision.
Demonstration: Read failing GitHub Actions log and create a proposed issue draft in test repo.

Stage name: Local Git, AST and LSP intelligence
Deliverable: Source-aware repository exploration
Acceptance checks: Rename/function reference lookup correct in fixtures; stale index invalidated on git commit; path outside workspace denied; binary and malformed files handled safely.
Demonstration: Locate definition, usages and tests of a method and produce a navigation graph.

Deliverable: Normalized verification runner
Acceptance checks: A planted vulnerability/test failure is detected; changed test definition invalidates prior success; absence of mandatory checker fails; no secret in logs; no automatic network dependency download unless allowed.
Demonstration: Run verified code quality profile against a controlled faulty sample project.

Deliverable: Artifact-bound proposed changes with CI feedback loop
Acceptance checks: Wrong base hash or stale contract blocks write; required checks cannot be deleted to pass; fake CI success rejected; branch creation/write requires explicit scope; output includes patch provenance.
Demonstration: Repair a failing fixture, open draft PR in test repository and record CI outcome.

Stage name: Safe SQL and analytical data adapters
Deliverable: PostgreSQL, SQLite and DuckDB read/query interfaces
Acceptance checks: RLS cross-workspace query fails; SQL injection and multi-statement mutation rejected; explain cost-limit works; raw DSN never exposed; queries interrupted on budget.
Demonstration: Query workspace-owned fixture and join CSV/Parquet with DuckDB.

Deliverable: Hybrid retrieval and semantic graph capability
Acceptance checks: Cross-tenant leakage absent under 100 adversarial queries; wrong embedding model revision cannot silently mix vectors; graph traversal respects max depth; search results reproduce from snapshot.
Demonstration: Return semantic and structural matches for a coding question.

Deliverable: API catalog generated from OpenAPI/GraphQL/gRPC schemas
Acceptance checks: Breaking API schema change blocks invocation until requalified; rate-limit fallback emits status; idempotency-key write behavior validated; provider errors correctly mapped.
Demonstration: Import OpenAPI spec and perform safe request using generated capability.

Stage name: Cloud, files, collaboration and optional services
Deliverable: Policy-controlled specialist connector profile
Acceptance checks: Each added connector passes standard contract suite; unavailable authorization reported accurately; cloud destructive action denied by default; cross-workspace secrets isolated.
Demonstration: Enable one chosen optional connector from registry and run qualification script.

Deliverable: Reasoning compute profile with Python/NumPy/SciPy/SymPy
Acceptance checks: Curated numeric/symbolic gold tasks meet exact/tolerance targets; NaN/overflow/ill-conditioned cases flagged; independent recomputation matches receipts; no untrusted wheel network install.
Demonstration: Solve sample analytical task both symbolically and numerically.

Deliverable: Z3/cvc5 and OR-Tools reasoning capabilities
Acceptance checks: Known SAT/UNSAT suites return correct outcome; timeout never recast as UNSAT; no untrusted solver expressions executed as Python; constraint model provenance retained.
Demonstration: Identify contradiction in cryptographic key-rotation rules and show counterexample.

Deliverable: Advanced computational backend with fallbacks
Acceptance checks: No paid API calls without budget authorization; inconsistent symbolic results trigger verification; units/dimensional checks pass; reproducibility report notes external provider version.
Demonstration: Compute same integral or optimization using two backends and compare.

Deliverable: Proof-checking and state-machine analysis profile
Acceptance checks: One true theorem checked, one deliberately false theorem rejected; flawed state-machine exposes counterexample; missing proof treated unverified; proof artifact retains checker revision.
Demonstration: Check no-double-dispatch invariant on a simplified tool queue state machine.

Deliverable: Type-directed workflow graph assembler
Acceptance checks: 50 golden dataflow cases compile; incompatible types rejected; cycles without bounds rejected; every edge carries immutable type/version; unauthorized transform cannot trigger a tool.
Demonstration: Compose SearchQuery → Pages → Claims → VerifiedReport without naming specific adapters.

Deliverable: Resumable DAG executor and event stream
Acceptance checks: Kill workers at 5 fault points and require no double side effects; event cursor replay identical after restart; fan-in waits for all required verified inputs; budget exhaustion halts safely.
Demonstration: Run fan-out multi-source research workflow with injected worker crash.

Stage name: Model reasoning controller and independent critics
Deliverable: Tool-aware reasoning and independent challenge workflow
Acceptance checks: Planted false claims challenged, unsupported conclusions labeled; reviewer cannot self-approve writes; no added model call bypasses budget; role context isolation passes.
Demonstration: Run same coding problem with and without tool/critic loop and compare verified outcomes.

Stage name: Adaptive selection, caching and capability utility
Prerequisites: T10.3; offline utility fixture (expanded by T11.1)
Deliverable: Policy-safe empirically learned router
Acceptance checks: Forced override honored; no unqualified tool promoted automatically; wrong-scope cache never served; with evidence insufficient route remains baseline rather than inventing performance gain.
Demonstration: Display a tool-selection decision explanation and its evidence.

Deliverable: Versioned baseline/gold dataset and blind task splits
Acceptance checks: At least 20 tasks per target domain to start with explicit difficulty and expected observable outcome; benchmark contamination checked; each outcome independently scored.
Demonstration: Produce model-only versus single-tool versus composite-tool comparison report.

Deliverable: Evidence checker and provenance audit
Acceptance checks: Tampered citation/patch/proof hash detected; unsupported claims fail; stale docs flagged; reproducible receipts for offline tasks; partial tool success not promoted to verified claim.
Demonstration: Show accepted claim, challenged claim and unresolved claim with source chain.

Deliverable: Comparable experiments and release regression gates
Acceptance checks: No aggregate metric mixes synthetic with live; baseline regressions fail gate at configured threshold; confidence uncertainty reported; all runs include pinned configs and costs.
Demonstration: Generate a CI report showing whether each tool meaningfully improves a target task family.

Deliverable: Red-team and failure-injection release suite
Acceptance checks: Zero critical successful boundary escapes in gated corpus; kill-switch works during incident; unqualified host fails closed; secrets absent in logs; data destruction requires explicit authorization.
Demonstration: Execute attack corpus in disposable CI environment and retain audit evidence.

Deliverable: Reproducible cross-platform deployment profiles
Acceptance checks: Fresh Linux install passes standard suite; Windows/macOS untrusted execution either passes qualified isolation or fails closed; offline smoke mode works without paid credentials; rollback documented.
Demonstration: Run fresh install and capability discovery from clean checkout.

Deliverable: Unified tool dashboard and API surfaces
Acceptance checks: Read-only users cannot approve; replay cursor shows same state after reconnect; all secret fields redacted; API and UI agree on execution status and verification state.
Demonstration: Operator inspects running workflow, approves a safe write and sees immutable result.

Stage name: Developer docs, SDK, examples and migration guides
Deliverable: Stable extension SDK and adoption documentation
Acceptance checks: External contributor can build a sample adapter following docs; examples run in CI; old project migrations preserve receipts and types; no unpinned download instructions.
Demonstration: Create sample custom tool using SDK and pass conformance tests.

Deliverable: Signed release with acceptance dossier and ongoing change control
Acceptance checks: All required tests pass on claimed hosts; no known critical security escape; release can be restored and receipts validated; metrics vs prior qualified version reported with no fabricated score.
Demonstration: Reproduce full gated demonstration from clean tagged checkout.
